html:
Jamaica became independent from Britain on 6 August 1962, the first British colony in the Caribbean to do so. Alexander Bustamante was its first prime minister.

Self rule had grown since the labour unrest of 1938 and the first universal suffrage election of 1944. Jamaica had joined the West Indies Federation but voted to leave it in 1961, which brought the federation down.

Independence came as bauxite mining and tourism were growing and as ska filled the dance halls. Many Jamaicans had already left for Britain since the Windrush of 1948. Under Michael Manley in the 1970s, the young state turned left, and its politics became violent.
sum: Jamaica became independent from Britain on 6 August 1962, the first British colony in the Caribbean to do so. Alexander Bustamante was its first prime minister.
